input.command:
cd /private/var/folders/kp/vdv61pd97vd0x29b257r8h7h0000gn/T/barcode-va1vsyp2; cat > /private/tmp/claude-501/-private-var-folders-kp-vdv61pd97vd0x29b257r8h7h0000gn-T-barcode-va1vsyp2/30b494ab-5396-4dc7-b160-8ed7e5b1f2d5/scratchpad/c.py <<'EOF'
import subprocess,numpy as np
from PIL import Image
b=np.array(Image.open('barcode.png').convert('RGB')).astype(float).mean(0)
N=len(b)
for L in 'ABCDEFGHIJ':
    out=subprocess.run(['ffmpeg','-v','quiet','-i',f'videos/{L}.mp4','-vf','scale=1:1','-r','1','-f','rawvideo','-pix_fmt','rgb24','-'],capture_output=True).stdout
    a=np.frombuffer(out,np.uint8).reshape(-1,3).astype(float)
    idx=np.linspace(0,len(a)-1,N).astype(int)
    v=a[idx]
    print(L,len(a),np.abs(v-b).mean())
EOF

content.text:
I sampled one frame per second from each of the ten videos, averaged each frame down to a single color, stretched the result to the barcode's width and measured how far it was from the barcode. A lower score means a closer match:

| Video | Avg. color difference |
|---|---|
| **B: Waka Waka** | **19.0** |
| I: Sin Pijama | 32.5 |
| G: Calma (Remix) | 36.7 |
| E: Bum Bum Tam Tam | 38.2 |
| others | 43–66 |

Waka Waka matches far better than any other video. The barcode's warm, earthy browns and greens also fit its look.

Answer: B
